title: Case 003: The Human Premium
requirement: Unlocks after two Archive decisions are recorded.
tests: Whether human-origin attention becomes a luxury product.
lesson: Human care becomes a luxury when synthetic care becomes default.
summary: Investigate a care platform where verified human attention is sold as an upgrade.

witnesses.Publish: Nia's case creates pressure. Vulnerable users fear becoming evidence.
witnesses.Bury: Nia's family remains protected. Kindred's tiered care market remains intact.
witnesses.Preserve: Jessa and Human Plus workers gain consent-protected channels into the Archive.

Publish.name: Jessa Calder
Publish.note: Jessa's words travel widely, but public attention begins simplifying Nia into a symbol.
Publish.lead: Public pressure may surface sponsor contracts, but family trust becomes fragile.

Bury.name: Kindred Basic Users
Bury.note: Raw care records remain private, but users keep living inside a system the Archive chose not to expose.
Bury.lead: Future evidence may arrive through anonymous user fragments rather than official records.

Preserve.name: Mara S.
Preserve.note: A timed and scored human listener offers labor evidence under anti-retaliation protections.
Preserve.lead: Worker testimony points toward deleted care records and erased escalation queues.

Publish.title: Public Human Plus allocation evidence
Publish.why: It makes the human paywall undeniable while risking intimate care records becoming spectacle.

Bury.title: Suppressed Kindred care-tier finding
Bury.why: It protects vulnerable users and Nia's family while allowing tiered care markets to keep defining the story.

Preserve.title: Restricted labor-and-care archive
Preserve.why: It preserves allocation proof without making the poor expose their worst moments to prove they deserved a human.

Publish.lead: Kindred sponsors begin deleting care-allocation records from legacy systems.

Bury.lead: A Basic user contacts the Archive because their companion keeps quoting Nia's case language.

Preserve.lead: Deleted Kindred logs point toward a larger erased-care archive.
